root_cause.text: The `drm_compat_ioctl` function in the DRM subsystem failed to mitigate Spectre v1 vulnerabilities by allowing speculative execution to access the `drm_compat_ioctls` function pointer array using an index derived from untrusted user input.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies `drivers/gpu/drm/drm_ioc32.c` to include `<linux/nospec.h>` and invokes `array_index_nospec(nr, ARRAY_SIZE(drm_compat_ioctls))` immediately before accessing `drm_compat_ioctls[nr]`, addressing the commit message's description of the "signature method of spectre problems" where user-controlled input dereferences a function pointer table.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement directly indexes into the drm_compat_ioctls function pointer array using 'cmd' which is derived from untrusted user input. Without proper Spectre v1 mitigation (such as array_index_nospec()), this allows speculative execution to access out-of-bounds memory locations when cmd exceeds valid array bounds, enabling information disclosure attacks.
